observations.text: SP, due to a late turn initiation with insufficient bank, did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain position during the tactical turns on the low-level route. Line abreast deviation reached 45 degrees and lateral separation deviated by 1600 feet from the briefed spacing, both beyond the code 1 tolerances of 30 degrees and 1000 feet. The IP directed the correction and flew part of the rollout to re-establish the tactical formation position.

SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the visual signals used in a comm-out turn, did not initiate the tactical turn at the briefed point and did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace during the turn. Altitude decayed 800 feet below the route altitude and exit speed was 40 knots low, beyond the code 1 tolerances of 500 feet low and 30 knots. The IP took control to ensure a safe altitude for maneuvering over the terrain and directed the re-establishment of the tactical formation position.

SP executed the tactical turns to the standard required for this Training Section, initiating each turn on the visual signal of No. 1 and rolling out in tactical formation position. Deviations reached the code 1 tolerances, with the rollout 30 degrees off the briefed recovery heading and lateral separation deviating by 1000 feet, and were corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the line abreast picture is expected to reduce the reliance on prompts.

SP executed the tactical turns with the briefed geometry, checking the corresponding responsibility airspace during each turn and applying the correction technique in order to remain in tactical formation position. Line abreast deviation stayed within 20 degrees, lateral separation within 800 feet and exit speed within 22 knots, with every deviation recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the tactical turns as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, exploiting and converting the A/C energy in order to maintain position and rolling out in tactical formation position. Line abreast deviation remained within 8 degrees, lateral separation within 350 feet, the rollout within 6 degrees of the briefed recovery heading and continuous G within 0.3 of the briefed value. Clearing and the responsibility airspace check were executed throughout each turn, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the tactical turns with exceptional accuracy, taking the initiative for safe separation and rolling out precisely in tactical formation position on every turn of the route. Deviations were negligible: line abreast within 3 degrees, lateral separation within 100 feet, recovery heading within 2 degrees, altitude within 60 feet and continuous G within 0.1 of the briefed value. The engine was used with consideration to the fuel reserve and the visual signals were executed without error. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt and over-controlled pull at the turn entry, did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain position during the tactical turns. Continuous G varied by 1.6 from the briefed value and exit speed was 50 knots low, beyond the code 1 tolerances of 1.0 G and 30 knots. The IP intervened, flew part of the recovery and directed the re-establishment of the tactical formation position.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the A/C position relative to the route turning point, did not take initiative for safe separation during the tactical turn and did not roll out in tactical formation position. The rollout was 45 degrees off the briefed recovery heading and lateral separation deviated by 1300 feet from the briefed spacing, beyond the code 1 tolerances of 30 degrees and 1000 feet. The IP directed the repositioning and flew part of the correction back onto the planned track.

SP, due to a delayed power addition at the turn exit, did not apply the correction technique required to remain in tactical formation position. Exit speed deviated by 30 knots and altitude by 1000 feet high, at the code 1 tolerances. Position on the route was regained only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the energy deficit was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated the navigation timing check inside the turn, did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace during the turn and did not maintain the briefed line abreast picture. Line abreast deviation reached 30 degrees and the rollout was 30 degrees off the briefed recovery heading, at the code 1 tolerances. The turns were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the deviations recognized and corrected with delay.

SP executed the tactical turns within the desired standards, checking the corresponding responsibility airspace and applying the correction technique in order to remain in tactical formation position. Line abreast deviation twice reached 20 degrees and lateral separation deviated by 750 feet, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier energy management at the turn entry is expected to improve position keeping on the route.

SP executed the tactical turns as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, exploiting and converting the A/C energy in order to maintain position on each leg of the route. Lateral separation remained within 400 feet, line abreast deviation within 9 degrees, exit speed within 12 knots and altitude within 300 feet of the route altitude, without IP's intervention. Clearing and a safe altitude for maneuvering over the high ground were ensured throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the tactical turns with exceptional accuracy, taking the initiative for safe separation and rolling out precisely in tactical formation position. Deviations were negligible: lateral separation within 100 feet, line abreast within 3 degrees, recovery heading within 2 degrees, exit speed within 4 knots and continuous G within 0.1 of the briefed value. The visual signals for the comm-out turns were executed without error and the engine was used with consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect crossing technique with the pull initiated below the briefed altitude, did not ensure a safe altitude for maneuvering over the high ground during the cross turn. Altitude reached 900 feet below the route altitude and lateral separation deviated by 1500 feet, beyond the code 1 tolerances of 500 feet low and 1000 feet. The IP took control, recovered the A/C to the route altitude and directed the re-establishment of the tactical formation position.

SP, due to an attention bottleneck on the navigation display at the expense of the visual lookout, did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace during the turn and did not take initiative for safe separation. Line abreast deviation reached 50 degrees and the rollout was 40 degrees off the briefed recovery heading, beyond the code 1 tolerances of 30 degrees for both parameters. The IP directed the correction and flew part of the turn to restore the tactical formation position.

SP, due to an inadequate lead point selection in the shackle turn, did not apply the correction technique required to remain in tactical formation position. The rollout was 30 degrees off the briefed recovery heading and lateral separation deviated by 1000 feet, at the code 1 tolerances. The tactical formation position was regained only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the deviation recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to failure to pass the required call at the briefed turn point, did not initiate the tactical turn in coordination with No. 1 and did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain position. Exit speed deviated by 30 knots and continuous G by 1.0 from the briefed value, at the code 1 tolerances. The turn was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the position was regained with delay.

SP, due to a slightly under-banked entry in the in place turns, did not hold the briefed line abreast picture through the rollout. Line abreast deviation reached 18 degrees and lateral separation deviated by 700 feet, between the code 3 and code 1 tolerances. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by the timing check on the navigation leg, did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace during the first hook turn and delayed the rollout. The rollout was 20 degrees off the briefed recovery heading and altitude reached 700 feet above the route altitude, between the code 3 and code 1 tolerances. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP executed the tactical turns within the desired standards, checking the corresponding responsibility airspace and rolling out in tactical formation position on each turn of the route. Line abreast deviation twice reached 9 degrees, lateral separation 480 feet and exit speed 14 knots, at the edge of the code 3 tolerances, without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent lead point and earlier power correction at the turn exit are expected to improve.

SP executed the tactical turns with exceptional accuracy as No. 1 and as No. 2, taking the initiative for safe separation and ensuring a safe altitude for maneuvering over the high ground. Deviations were negligible: line abreast within 3 degrees, lateral separation within 100 feet, recovery heading within 2 degrees, exit speed within 5 knots, altitude within 60 feet and continuous G within 0.1 of the briefed value. The visual signals were executed without error in the comm-out turns and the engine was used with consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.
